JOB

Turn light measurements into an explanation of what is in the air.

CLASS QUESTION

How can you find an invisible gas from space?
title: Atmospheric science and remote sensing

text:
WORK
Check the signal

Decide whether a measurement is reliable, or caused by something else such as cloud or a bright surface.

Build an estimate

Use models and wind information to turn an absorption signal into a rate of emission.

Share the findings

Explain results, and their uncertainty, to people who make decisions.
title: Atmospheric science and remote sensing

text:
WHY

GHGSat

Methane leaks from industrial sites are invisible and were mostly self-reported. GHGSat says that when it started in 2011, 75% of industrial emissions had no independent monitoring.

GHGSat describes itself as a greenhouse gas emissions intelligence company. It uses its own satellites and aircraft to measure methane from industrial sites around the world. It says it has launched 16 satellites.

JOB

Find out whether an intervention helps a wild population recover.

CLASS QUESTION

Can helping individual owls help a population recover?
title: Conservation research and population ecology

text:
WORK
Plan a comparison

Choose measures of survival, breeding and population change, and decide what to compare them with.

Follow animals after release

Record observations over time, accounting for animals that are difficult to detect.

Interpret the evidence

Ask whether results reflect the intervention, environmental conditions or other explanations.
title: Conservation research and population ecology

text:
WHY

Wilder Institute

At-risk species need support that addresses survival, habitat and the challenges of returning animals to the wild. The burrowing owl program focuses on vulnerable young birds.

Wilder describes itself as a global conservation charity bringing together conservation, animal care and public engagement. Its work includes the Calgary Zoo and species recovery programs.

Observed in a 2025 researcher interview
